title: Coordinator Receipts, Broadcast, and Assignment Constraints PRD
executive_summary: Widen worker-signal receipts to all signal types, replace the dead broadcast target with a per-seat fan-out, and stamp a CONSTRAINTS block on every WORK_ASSIGNMENT dispatch.

functional_requirements.description: QF-20260906-162 shipped writeSignalReceipts() in scripts/fleet-dashboard.cjs, gated to payload.signal_type==='stuck' AND payload.severity==='high', with its receipt-existence-check bounded at .limit(50) on the premise that printInbox()'s .limit(20) batch could only ever produce 1-2 stuck+high rows. Remove the stuck+high filter so every worker signal in printInbox()'s enumerated batch gets one signal_receipt row via dispatchToWorker, still correlation_id-idempotent. Since removing the filter widens the batch toward the full 20, the existence-check bound MUST be derived from the enumerated batch's own length (e.g. Math.max(highStuckSignals.length, 50) or paginate via fapPaginate), never a fixed literal that a future batch-widening could exceed -- the same rule FR-5(d) imposes on its gauge applies here at the write site itself. Add a rendered disposition line ('queued' | 'routed:<target>' | 'needs-decision:<who>') into the outbound row's Subject or Details text -- coordination-inbox.cjs's render (line 822 Subject, line 823 Details) has no generic payload-field render, so the line must go in one of those two fields, not a bare payload key. Add 'signal_receipt' to INFORMATIONAL_KINDS (lib/fleet/worker-status.cjs) alongside its existing BACKPRESSURE_EXEMPT_KINDS membership -- this is a DELIBERATE dual membership (classifyCoordinationRow checks INFORMATIONAL_KINDS before the drain-set union, so the kind classifies informational despite also being drainable via the exempt-kind spread) and is the SAME dual-membership pattern signal_receipt already has today; it is not an accident to guard against here, only to record. Adam-advisory receipts and coordinator_request rows are explicitly OUT of this FR: coordinator_request rows carry no payload.signal_type and cannot appear in printInbox()'s signal_type-filtered batch at all (widening the enumeration query to include them is a separate, unscoped change flagged by the code's own comment that it would surface 105+ unrelated INFO rows), and Adam-advisory widening remains cut per the LEAD-phase deletion audit (unbounded duplicate-write risk, filed as a follow-up QF).
functional_requirements.requirement: Widen the existing signal-receipt write site to every worker /signal row (not just stuck+high) and render a disposition line, with an existence-check bound sized to the full batch
acceptance_criteria: AC-1: a worker signal of any signal_type/severity enumerated in writeSignalReceipts' input batch produces exactly one signal_receipt row correlated to it, verified by calling writeSignalReceipts directly with an injected client (its own docblock: extracted specifically for direct unit testability, unlike printInbox which takes no client) and asserting a second call with the same batch writes zero additional rows

AC-2: the receipt row's rendered Subject or Details text (per coordination-inbox.cjs's actual render, not the payload object) contains one of 'queued', 'routed:', or 'needs-decision:' as a literal substring

AC-3: signal_receipt is present in BOTH lib/fleet/worker-status.cjs INFORMATIONAL_KINDS and BACKPRESSURE_EXEMPT_KINDS, and a stub-supabase test with 3 pre-existing unanswered rows on a target plus a new signal_receipt send does not trigger DISPATCH_SEND_BACKPRESSURE_REFUSED

AC-17: a batch of 20 enumerated worker signals (exceeding the old literal 50-row existence-check bound's original 1-2-row premise) still writes exactly one receipt per signal, with zero duplicates, when the existence check is re-run against the same 20-row batch

AC-18: the INFORMATIONAL_KINDS+BACKPRESSURE_EXEMPT_KINDS dual membership for signal_receipt (and any future kind added the same way) is confined to an explicit, named allowlist constant, so an unintentional future overlap between the two lists fails a CI assertion rather than passing silently

functional_requirements.description: The originally-specified target_session='broadcast' sentinel has zero worker readers. Build a new module (lib/coordinator/capped-pool-broadcast.cjs) that: (a) reads the live worktree count via countActiveWorktrees()/MAX_WORKTREE_COUNT (lib/worktree-quota.js, ESM, imported dynamically from the CJS coordinator tick); (b) when over cap for more than 30 minutes (configurable), enumerates live seats via liveFleetSessions() (lib/fleet/live-fleet-sessions.cjs) and sends ONE directed INFO row per seat, all sharing one run_id, payload.kind='capped_pool_broadcast'; (c) adds capped_pool_broadcast to PAYLOAD_KINDS, INFORMATIONAL_KINDS, and BOTH copies of BACKPRESSURE_EXEMPT_KINDS (lib/coordinator/dispatch.cjs:39's Set AND lib/fleet/worker-status.cjs:229's frozen array -- two separate constants, both must be updated) plus the corresponding role_drain_sets migration (since BACKPRESSURE_EXEMPT_KINDS is spread into every role's DRAIN_SET, making the kind ackable/drainable by every seat -- this is why the dedupe design below CANNOT use acknowledged_at); (d) DEDUPES FIRE-ONCE ON EMISSION RECENCY, NOT ACKNOWLEDGEMENT: because the kind becomes drainable and any seat can ack its own copy, an acknowledged_at IS NULL dedupe (the emitReaperStarvationAlert pattern) would self-clear the instant one seat drains its row, causing a duplicate broadcast on the very next tick even though nothing changed. Instead, dedupe by selecting whether a row of the same kind for that target was created within the re-emit window (created_at > now - 6h), using the reaper-tick-style state file (scripts/fleet/worktree-reaper-tick.cjs readState/writeState) to track the over-cap-since timestamp and the last-emitted-at time per run, independent of any seat's ack state; (e) emits one additional 'cleared' notice (payload.cleared=true discriminator on the same kind) the first tick the condition resolves, using the same recency-based dedupe.
functional_requirements.requirement: Replace the dead target_session='broadcast' capped-pool-broadcast mechanism with a per-live-seat directed fan-out, deduped by emission recency rather than acknowledgement state
acceptance_criteria: AC-4: with a live worktree count above MAX_WORKTREE_COUNT for a simulated 31 minutes, exactly one directed INFO row per currently-live seat is produced, and a second tick within the 6h window produces zero additional rows for the same condition
AC-5: when the over-cap condition clears, exactly one additional per-seat notice is sent on the next tick, and zero further notices after that

AC-6: tests/unit/fleet/drain-set-registry.test.js's exact seed-row-count assertion (106 -> 110) and tests/unit/fleet/drain-sets-adam-reconciliation.test.js's per-role count assertions are updated to the new totals and pass; the new migration is added to RECONCILIATION_MIGRATION_PATHS

AC-19: a target that has acknowledged (drained) its capped_pool_broadcast row still receives ZERO additional broadcast rows on the next tick within the re-emit window -- the dedupe is provably independent of any seat's ack state, not merely untested against it

functional_requirements.description: CORRECTED at EXEC (evidence 4298bd82-d59d-4ac6-b585-eb6aaf206915): the original FR-3 widened the shared resolveHoldProvenance (lib/fleet/claim-eligibility.cjs) with four new keys (human_action_note, human_action_reason, human_action_required, needs_coordinator_review_reason). EXEC-phase TESTING found this had an unaudited, fleet-wide consequence: resolveHoldProvenance is not purely descriptive -- scripts/post-merge-handoff-orchestrator.js's classifyState() and lib/fleet/belt-census.cjs both gate real behavior (auto-handoff refusal, belt census bucketing) on whatever it resolves, and the widening moved 64 live SDs into a newly-resolved hold, 11 non-terminal, stalling their auto-handoff -- permanently, since none of the four keys had a release-check path. resolveHoldProvenance is REVERTED to its original 6-key precedence chain (requires_human_action_reason, not_worker_claimable_reason, review_hold_reason, dispatch_ineligible_reason, pilot_throwaway, deferred_by); the HOLD_REASON_KEYS export is removed. Instead, stampConstraintsBlock (lib/coordinator/dispatch.cjs) reads the four keys DIRECTLY -- the same pattern already used there for the solomon_* fields -- rendering each as its own CONSTRAINTS line (with the same control-char sanitization applied to every other rendered field) with zero effect on any dispatch/handoff/belt gate. QF-20260904-724's ORIGINAL problem (the dashboard rendering 5 specific SDs' holds as 'no reason recorded (bare flag)') remains UNFIXED by this SD -- that is a genuinely separate fix (widening the DASHBOARD's own render path, or resolveHoldProvenance itself after a full consumer audit this SD did not have scope to perform) and QF-20260904-724 should stay open for a session that does that audit properly.
functional_requirements.requirement: Surface four governance-note metadata keys directly inside stampConstraintsBlock, WITHOUT widening the shared resolveHoldProvenance
acceptance_criteria: AC-7: stampConstraintsBlock renders a distinct CONSTRAINTS line for metadata carrying only human_action_note, only human_action_reason, only needs_coordinator_review_reason (real text each), and for metadata carrying only human_action_required=true (a fixed 'Human action required: true' line) -- verified against the actual rendered row.body, not a mocked stamper call

AC-20 (regression guard): resolveHoldProvenance(metadata) returns null for metadata carrying ONLY one of the four keys above -- proving the shared, gate-affecting resolver was NOT widened, so scripts/post-merge-handoff-orchestrator.js's classifyState() and lib/fleet/belt-census.cjs see byte-identical behavior to before this SD

AC-9 (scope note, no longer a drift-detection test): this SD does not attempt to make QF-20260904-724's original dashboard bare-flag problem self-detecting, since fixing it requires a consumer audit outside this SD's scope; QF-20260904-724 remains open

functional_requirements.description: buildWorkAssignment does not exist; the real choke point is insertCoordinationRow (lib/coordinator/dispatch.cjs:1214), which runs three fail-soft stamper guards keyed on message_type==='WORK_ASSIGNMENT'. Add a fourth, stampConstraintsBlock(supabase, row, logger), following the identical fail-soft pattern: resolve the target SD's ratifications_cited, forbidden-framings text, hold provenance via resolveHoldProvenance/formatHoldProvenance (post-FR-3), and any Solomon-ruling text; render as a 'CONSTRAINTS:' block. THE STAMP WRITES THE IDENTICAL RENDERED STRING TO BOTH row.body AND row.payload.body DIRECTLY (never relying on the existing fill-if-absent mirrors at lines 1468 and 1477 to propagate it to the other field) -- dispatch.cjs has TWO such mirrors (payload.body->body at 1468, body->payload.body at 1477), and a caller who set both fields before this stamp runs would leave one copy stale if the stamp only touched one; writing both directly removes the ordering dependency on either mirror entirely. Apply the existing capBodySafe (lib/shared/body-cap.cjs) to the rendered block BEFORE merging it into the body. WHEN capBodySafe REPORTS BODY_TOO_LONG (it returns {value:null, error}, never throws, never truncates): fail soft, exactly like the other three stampers on any other error -- drop the CONSTRAINTS stamp for that dispatch, log a loud warning naming the SD and the oversized-block byte length, and let the un-stamped WORK_ASSIGNMENT insert proceed unblocked. Do NOT throw and refuse the insert (that would contradict the sibling stampers' contract and turn a formatting overflow into a dispatch outage). When no constraint resolves, the block reads 'CONSTRAINTS: none recorded' -- rendered only when the resolver genuinely found nothing (never omitted, and never rendered as 'none recorded' merely because one key failed to match while others were never checked).
functional_requirements.requirement: Stamp a CONSTRAINTS block on every WORK_ASSIGNMENT dispatch, writing both body fields directly and failing soft on an oversized render
acceptance_criteria: AC-10: a WORK_ASSIGNMENT dispatched for an SD carrying metadata.ratifications_cited and a review_hold_reason produces a body containing a 'CONSTRAINTS:' section naming both, verified against the actual inserted row
AC-11: a WORK_ASSIGNMENT dispatched for an SD with no constraint-bearing metadata keys produces a body containing 'CONSTRAINTS: none recorded'

AC-12: for a caller that pre-sets BOTH row.body and row.payload.body before insertCoordinationRow runs, after the stamp executes both fields are byte-identical and BOTH contain the CONSTRAINTS block -- proving the stamp writes both copies directly rather than relying on either fill-if-absent mirror

AC-13: when the rendered CONSTRAINTS block would push the body over BODY_HARD_CAP (4096), the WORK_ASSIGNMENT insert still SUCCEEDS with the un-stamped body and a logged warning (fail-soft), not a thrown error and not a truncated block

functional_requirements.description: Per ratification 49656c8c's preventive-exit-predicate requirement: (a) drain fixtures (extending tests/unit/coordinator/fleet-dashboard-signal-receipt.test.js) per FR-1's ACs; (b) pool-over-cap fixtures per FR-2's ACs, explicitly including the acked-target-still-suppressed case (AC-19); (c) assignment fixtures per FR-4's ACs, including the both-fields-set case (AC-12) and the oversized-body fail-soft case (AC-13); (d) a gauge (extending lib/fleet/outstanding-signals.cjs's existing 'received' predicate, currently bounded at a literal .limit(20)) counting worker signals older than 30 minutes with no correlated signal_receipt row, asserted at zero from the merge commit, with its existence-check query bound derived from the enumerated result set's own length via the existing fapPaginate helper (never a fixed literal), and its fail-soft catch reporting unknown/error rather than a false-pass zero on a lookup failure.
functional_requirements.requirement: CI fixtures asserting each mechanism above, plus a zero-asserted unreceipted-signal gauge
acceptance_criteria: AC-14: `npx vitest run --project unit` passes with the new fixtures included, and the existing 113-test baseline (captured in .artifacts/testing-plan-to-exec-receipts-broadcast-run.json, matching the LEAD-phase artifact byte-for-byte) still passes unchanged

AC-15: the FR-5(d) gauge reports 0 unreceipted signals older than 30 minutes when run against a fixture with N synthetic signals all carrying receipts, reports N (not 0) when the receipts are removed, and reports 'unknown' (not 0) when the query is made to throw

AC-16: tests/unit/coordination/kind-classification.test.js's informational/actionable disjointness assertion still passes after signal_receipt and capped_pool_broadcast are added to INFORMATIONAL_KINDS, AND a new, separately-asserted overlap check confirms that any kind present in BOTH INFORMATIONAL_KINDS and an effective role DRAIN_SET is a member of the explicit dual-membership allowlist from AC-18 (so the existing disjointness test's structural inability to catch this overlap, per its own before-drain-set-union precedence, is compensated by a check that CAN)

technical_requirements.rationale: TST-B4 found the mirror is fill-if-absent in BOTH directions; a stamper appending to row.body after the mirror already ran leaves row.payload.body stale for any reader keyed on the payload side, silently diverging the two copies of the same message.
technical_requirements.requirement: stampConstraintsBlock must execute before dispatch.cjs's body/payload.body fill-if-absent mirror (line 1468), not after

technical_requirements.rationale: INFORMATIONAL_KINDS changes need no migration (that list is not spread into role_drain_sets), but BACKPRESSURE_EXEMPT_KINDS IS spread into every role's drain set (worker-status.cjs DRAIN_SETS), so a code-only change without the migration+test updates leaves the four per-role counts and the exact-106 seed-row assertion failing, exactly as QF-20260906-162's own migration (20260906_role_drain_sets_add_signal_receipt.sql) had to do.
technical_requirements.requirement: Any new BACKPRESSURE_EXEMPT_KINDS entry (capped_pool_broadcast) must ship its role_drain_sets migration, seed-count test update, and per-role count test update in the SAME PR as the code change

technical_requirements.rationale: scripts/fleet/worktree-reaper-tick.cjs already duplicates this constant as a documented workaround ('cannot require the ESM quota module'); FR-2's new module should use dynamic import instead so the two constants cannot drift, which is the exact defect class (a coalescer's key list and its writers' keys diverging) this whole SD exists to close elsewhere.
technical_requirements.requirement: lib/worktree-quota.js (ESM) must be read via dynamic import() from the CommonJS coordinator tick, never duplicated as a second MAX_WORKTREE_COUNT constant

technical_requirements.rationale: A second live-seat enumeration with even slightly different freshness-window semantics than the one used elsewhere in the fleet (worker-status.cjs FLEET_ACTIVE_WINDOW_MS-based checks) would broadcast to a subtly different seat population than every other liveness-gated surface, reintroducing the exact instrument-disagreement class this SD's rationale names.
technical_requirements.requirement: The FR-2 fan-out must reuse liveFleetSessions() (lib/fleet/live-fleet-sessions.cjs), not re-derive a live-seat set independently

system_architecture: {"overview":"Four independent write-path changes converge on the coordinator's existing coordination_row dispatch machinery: FR-1 widens an existing enumeration-time write site, FR-2 adds a new tick-driven fan-out writer, FR-3 patches a shared read helper, and FR-4 adds a fourth stamper guard at the one choke point every dispatch already passes through. No new tables, no new comms lane -- every write still lands in session_coordination via the existing insertCoordinationRow/dispatchToWorker path.","components":[{"name":"writeSignalReceipts (widened)","responsibility":"Enumerate every worker signal in the current printInbox() batch and write one correlation_id-idempotent signal_receipt row per signal via dispatchToWorker, with a rendered disposition line","technology":"Node.js CJS, scripts/fleet-dashboard.cjs"},{"name":"capped-pool-broadcast module (new)","responsibility":"Tick-driven: read live worktree count vs cap, and when over-cap past the hold window, fan out one directed INFO row per live seat with fire-once dedupe and a cleared-notice transition","technology":"Node.js CJS, new lib/coordinator/capped-pool-broadcast.cjs, invoked from scripts/stale-session-sweep.cjs's existing tick"},{"name":"resolveHoldProvenance (widened)","responsibility":"Resolve a hold's reason text from any of the now-10 documented metadata keys, in a fixed precedence order, respecting release state","technology":"Node.js CJS, lib/fleet/claim-eligibility.cjs"},{"name":"stampConstraintsBlock (new)","responsibility":"Fourth stamper guard at insertCoordinationRow: render ratifications, holds, and rulings into the WORK_ASSIGNMENT body before the body-mirror fill-if-absent runs, capped by capBodySafe","technology":"Node.js CJS, lib/coordinator/dispatch.cjs"}],"data_flow":"A worker signal or advisory lands in session_coordination -> the coordinator's inbox-core render (printInbox/printAdamInbox) enumerates it each tick -> writeSignalReceipts fires a correlated signal_receipt row back to the sender, exempt from backpressure and drain-set-recognized as informational on all four roles. Separately, the coordinator's periodic sweep tick reads the live worktree count -> capped-pool-broadcast decides whether to fan out, using the existing session_coordination table itself (via an existing-unacknowledged-row select) as its own dedupe state, no new table. Separately again, any WORK_ASSIGNMENT insert passes through insertCoordinationRow -> the new stampConstraintsBlock reads the target SD's metadata -> resolveHoldProvenance (widened) resolves any hold -> the rendered CONSTRAINTS text is merged into the body before the existing mirror runs.","integration_points":["session_coordination (all four write paths share this one table)","role_drain_sets (migration path for the new BACKPRESSURE_EXEMPT_KINDS entry)","strategic_directives_v2.metadata (read by both resolveHoldProvenance and stampConstraintsBlock)"]}
implementation_approach: {"phases":[{"phase":"Phase 1","description":"Land QF-20260904-724's resolveHoldProvenance widening plus its drift-detection test (FR-3), since FR-4 depends on it","deliverables":["resolveHoldProvenance key-list widening","drift-detection test","QF-20260904-724 marked completed"]},{"phase":"Phase 2","description":"Widen writeSignalReceipts (FR-1) and add the INFORMATIONAL_KINDS entry for signal_receipt","deliverables":["all-signal-types receipt write path","rendered disposition line","INFORMATIONAL_KINDS update"]},{"phase":"Phase 3","description":"Build the capped-pool-broadcast module (FR-2) and its role_drain_sets migration","deliverables":["lib/coordinator/capped-pool-broadcast.cjs","state-file persistence","migration + seed-count test updates"]},{"phase":"Phase 4","description":"Add the fourth stamper guard (FR-4) at insertCoordinationRow, ordered before the body mirror","deliverables":["stampConstraintsBlock","capBodySafe integration","CONSTRAINTS rendering"]},{"phase":"Phase 5","description":"CI fixtures for all four mechanisms plus the FR-5(d) gauge (FR-5)","deliverables":["updated fleet-dashboard-signal-receipt.test.js","new capped-pool-broadcast test","new constraints-block dispatch test","unreceipted-signal gauge + test"]}],"technical_decisions":["Keep the receipt shape as a NEW ROW (matching QF-20260906-162's shipped behavior) rather than the STEP-0 rider's originally-preferred UPDATE-with-receipted_at shape, since reverting merged production code to relitigate a shape preference is not warranted","Reuse lib/coordinator/coordination-events.cjs's fire-once dedupe pattern for FR-2 instead of inventing new dedupe machinery, per the SD's own 'no new machinery' rationale","Sequence FR-3 (the QF-724 prerequisite) before FR-4 within this SD's own EXEC rather than waiting on another session to pick up the unclaimed QF"]}

acceptance_criteria: Every worker signal enumerated by writeSignalReceipts receives exactly one correlation_id-idempotent signal_receipt row, regardless of signal_type/severity or batch size, with zero effect on the target's send-backpressure count

The over-cap fleet-wide notice reaches every live worker seat directly, fires at most once per 6h re-emit window regardless of any seat's acknowledgement state, and fires exactly once more when it clears

Every WORK_ASSIGNMENT dispatch carries a CONSTRAINTS block naming every resolvable ratification/hold/ruling on the target SD in both body and payload.body, rendering 'none recorded' only when genuinely none exist, and failing soft (never throwing) when the render exceeds the body cap

The four governance-note keys (human_action_note/human_action_reason/human_action_required/needs_coordinator_review_reason) reach the worker via the CONSTRAINTS block with zero effect on resolveHoldProvenance or any consumer that gates on it (auto-handoff, belt census) -- QF-20260904-724's original dashboard-display problem remains open for a separately-scoped fix

risks.risk: The over-cap trigger's own state (over-cap-since timestamp) could double-count or reset incorrectly across coordinator restarts if implemented as an in-memory value instead of a durable marker
risks.mitigation: Mirror scripts/fleet/worktree-reaper-tick.cjs's own readState/writeState JSON-file pattern (already reviewed, already in production) rather than inventing new persistence; the state file survives process restarts by design.
risks.rollback_plan: Delete the state file to reset the over-cap timer to 'not yet over cap'; the fan-out logic recomputes from a clean slate on the next tick with no data loss, since the fan-out rows themselves (not the timer) are the durable side-effect.

risks.risk: Widening BACKPRESSURE_EXEMPT_KINDS with a second entry (capped_pool_broadcast) in the same PR cycle as QF-20260904-695's counter fix could land in the wrong order and silently regress the exemption for one kind while fixing it for the other
risks.mitigation: This SD adds capped_pool_broadcast to BOTH BACKPRESSURE_EXEMPT_KINDS and INFORMATIONAL_KINDS independent of QF-20260904-695's landing order (mirroring how signal_receipt already sits in both after this SD's FR-1), so the exemption holds regardless of which PR merges first.
risks.rollback_plan: Revert the single migration + the two constant additions; no other code path depends on capped_pool_broadcast existing, so the revert is self-contained.

risks.risk: Adam-advisory receipts were cut from FR-1's scope (TST-B3's unbounded duplicate-write finding) but the underlying gap (Adam's signals also going un-receipted) remains open and could recur as a chairman-facing complaint before its own follow-up QF is filed
risks.mitigation: File the follow-up QF for Adam-advisory receipts as part of this SD's own completion tail, explicitly scoped to fix the write-site's query-window mismatch (raise the existence-check limit to match the 200-row fetch, or bound both to the same window) before shipping, rather than leaving it as an unowned gap.
risks.rollback_plan: N/A -- this is a scope-cut, not a shipped mechanism; there is nothing to roll back.

conditions.action: Resolve the conditions noted by the sub-agent before treating this CONDITIONAL_PASS as fully green

security_analysis.justification: CONDITIONAL_PASS recorded by SECURITY: Five of six reviewed surfaces are clean. The migration is purely additive, the new payload kinds grant only the documented backpressure exemption with every target, role and authorization guard still executing ahead of it, the broadcast state file has no traversal or attacker-influenced content, and the widened signal receipts stay parameterized and sender-scoped. One must-fix: the new CONSTRAINTS stamper renders three groups of metadata strings without the control-char stripping its own sibling hold path already applies, allowing a seat that can write SD metadata to forge governance lines in another worker's WORK_ASSIGNMENT. Proven by executed proof-of-concept. Roughly a four-line fix.. See the attached conditions, warnings, and recommendations for the specific follow-ups required before this verdict is treated as fully green.

key_decisions: Cut Adam-advisory receipts from FR-1 (unbounded duplicate-write risk found by prospective TESTING)
Redesigned FR-2's target from the dead 'broadcast' sentinel to a per-seat directed fan-out
Redirected FR-4's anchor from the nonexistent buildWorkAssignment to insertCoordinationRow
Folded QF-20260904-724 into this SD's own EXEC as a sequencing prerequisite rather than waiting on an unclaimed QF
patterns_identified: Fail-soft stamper guards at insertCoordinationRow, keyed on message_type==='WORK_ASSIGNMENT' (stampEffortRecommendation/stampModelRecommendation/stampPremiseMeasurement)
Fire-once dedupe by selecting an existing unacknowledged unexpired row of the same payload.kind before writing a new alert (emitReaperStarvationAlert)
A dual-list membership contract: INFORMATIONAL_KINDS (no migration) vs BACKPRESSURE_EXEMPT_KINDS (migration + seed-count test updates required, since it is spread into role_drain_sets)
